info.title: PuzzleQuest API
info.description:
PuzzleQuest's API, for its web pages and for apps. This description is at `/api/v1/openapi.json`, and shown as a reference at `/api/v1/docs`.

Sign in with `POST /sessions`. A browser keeps the session in a cookie; an app asks for its token (`"client": "native"`) and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A request that changes something and is sent with the cookie must come from this site.

Lists come a page at a time: `?limit=` (default 50, at most 200) and `?after=`, the `next` value of the page before.

Names and values follow the same conventions throughout. Things are named in paths and bodies as `questName`, `puzzleName`, `teamName`, and `userName`; a quest's stop is named by its puzzle's `puzzleName`. Enumerated values, such as statuses, roles, and event types, are camelCase strings. A field whose value isn't set, such as a time that hasn't come yet, is present with the value `null`; a field is absent only when the caller isn't allowed to see it, as each such field's description says. Units are in names: `timePenaltySeconds`, `elapsedMs`.

Version 1.0 can gain fields, enumerated values, problem types, and live-update messages without a new version. Clients must ignore fields they don't recognise, and treat a value they don't recognise sensibly, such as an unknown status as unknown, rather than failing. So the response schemas here don't forbid fields they don't list, though this version sends only the fields they list.

Clients follow a quest as it happens over the live-update websocket, `/api/v1/updates`. Anyone may connect. A client sends a `LiveUpdateSubscription` naming the quest, with a ticket from `POST /quests/{questName}/live-tickets`; the server answers with its connection's ID, then sends a `LiveUpdate` for each change to that quest, naming the puzzle concerned where there is one. A client sends its connection's ID as `connectionId` with its own actions, so their updates aren't sent back to it. Each update names the entry whose progress changed (`entryId`). While a quest is a race that not every entry has finished, a connection is sent an update's content only if its ticket was issued to staff, an administrator, or a player of that entry; every other connection is sent `questUpdated` with the entry's ID instead, and fetches what it shows again. Starting and resetting a quest send its followers `questUpdated`, as the puzzle master's other changes do; after a reset, the entry it names may no longer be there to fetch. A player's home screen instead names the user, with a ticket from `POST /users/{userName}/live-tickets`, and is sent `questsChanged` whenever the list of quests they play should be fetched again, starting and resetting included. Both messages are described under the schemas. Updates can be missed, so a client should fetch what it follows again each time it connects.

The puzzle master can send an entry's players messages, from the quest console. A message may set a challenge: a small puzzle whose answer the players send (`POST /quests/{questName}/challenge/answers`, or by text message), and whose confirmation, once they have it, they show the venue's staff. A player's quest shows its entry's `messages` and `challenge`; when either changes, the entry's players and staff following the quest are sent `messageSent` or `challengeAnswered`, and fetch it again. Players who have the app are sent each message as a push notification too.

An app gets push notifications by registering its phone with its session: `PUT /sessions/current/push-target`. They stop when the session ends. The server sends them to an entry's players, except whoever caused them: when the quest starts, is paused or resumed, when a teammate solves a stop, and, once every entry in a race has finished, where each came. What one carries is described under the schemas as `PushNotification`, and published with each release as `push-notifications.json`.

Errors are problem details (RFC 9457), sent as `application/problem+json`. Act on their `type`, one of:

| Type | Status | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/problems/invalid-request` | 400 | The request's parameters or body are missing, malformed, or have values that aren't allowed. The errors member lists each problem, with where it is, such as body.email. |
| `/problems/sign-in-required` | 401 | The request needs a signed-in user, and has no session, or one that has ended. |
| `/problems/sign-in-failed` | 401 | The user name and password don't match an account. Which of them is wrong isn't said. |
| `/problems/forbidden` | 403 | The signed-in user isn't allowed to do this. |
| `/problems/cross-site-request` | 403 | A request that changes something was sent with this site's cookie from a page on another site. Send it from this site, or with a Bearer token. |
| `/problems/not-found` | 404 | There is no such resource, or the signed-in user may not know about it. |
| `/problems/already-exists` | 409 | Something with that name, email address, or join code already exists, or the user is already a member of the team. |
| `/problems/email-not-verified` | 409 | The user hasn't verified their email address, so nothing can be sent to it that depends on it, such as a password reset link. |
| `/problems/incorrect-password` | 422 | The current password given isn't the user's password. |
| `/problems/password-not-allowed` | 422 | The new password doesn't meet the password policy, such as its length, or is the same as the current one. |
| `/problems/wrong-join-code` | 422 | The join code isn't the team's. |
| `/problems/invalid-link` | 422 | The token from a password reset or email verification link isn't valid: it is malformed, already used, or expired. |
| `/problems/in-use` | 409 | It can't be deleted while something uses it, such as a puzzle a quest includes. The detail says what uses it. |
| `/problems/invalid-upload` | 400 | The upload is missing a field, sends its fields in the wrong order, or is a kind of file that isn't accepted. |
| `/problems/body-too-large` | 413 | The request's body is larger than the server reads. |
| `/problems/upload-too-large` | 413 | The uploaded file is larger than allowed. |
| `/problems/invalid-quest` | 422 | The quest's entrants name a user or team that doesn't exist, or a player in more than one entry, or it lists a puzzle that doesn't exist or appears twice. |
| `/problems/wrong-state` | 409 | The quest or puzzle isn't in a state that allows this: for example, the quest has already started, isn't paused, or is completed, or the puzzle hasn't been reached or solved. The detail says which. |
| `/problems/quest-paused` | 409 | The puzzle master has paused the quest; the players can't act until it resumes. |
| `/problems/try-again` | 409 | Someone else changed the quest at the same moment, several times over. Try again. |
| `/problems/wrong-activation-code` | 422 | The activation code, typed or scanned, isn't the puzzle's. |
| `/problems/wrong-answer` | 422 | The guess isn't the puzzle's solution. |
| `/problems/no-recipients` | 409 | No player in the entries being texted has a phone number and accepts text messages. |
| `/problems/messaging-failed` | 502 | The text messaging service refused or failed to send a message. The details are logged. |
| `/problems/unreadable-qr-code` | 422 | No QR code could be read from the scanned image; try again, closer or with more light, or type the code. |
| `/problems/no-more-hints` | 409 | Every one of the puzzle's hints has been revealed. |
| `/problems/too-many-requests` | 429 | Too many attempts in a short time. The RateLimit and RateLimit-Policy headers say when to try again. |
| `/problems/unexpected` | 500 | Something went wrong on the server. The details are logged, not sent. |
| `about:blank` | 4xx | Any other HTTP error, such as a body that isn't valid JSON; the title is the status's. |

post.description: Starts a session. A browser ("web", the default) gets it as a cookie; an app ("native") gets its token in the response.

put.summary: Get push notifications on this phone
put.description: Sends the session's push notifications to the phone with this token, replacing any it was sending to; a token another session had moves to this one. They stop when the session ends: on signing out, its expiring, or its user's password changing. Apps send this whenever they're launched, since tokens change.

post.summary: Text every entrant's players
post.description: Sends the puzzle master's message to every entry in progress, as a team's or player's own address does (see there): kept with each entry and shown in the app, and texted to the players who accept texts, each number once. With an expected response, each of those entries waits for its own answer to the challenge. To message one team or player, use its own address.

message.description: What to send. Required, unless sending a kept challenge again by its challengeId.

responseConfirmation.description: What a right answer to the challenge shows the players, in the app or texted back, for them to show the venue's staff.

challengeId.description: To send one of the quest's kept challenges again, as it was kept (see GET /quests/{questName}/challenges), instead of a message.

post.description: With the users and teams playing it (at least one; a player may be in only one of them), and its puzzles in order; each puzzle gets an activation code unless one is given, the same for every entrant.

visibility.description: Who can follow the quest: anyone, or only its players (in any of its entries) and staff. New quests are public.

textPlayersWithApp.description: Whether the puzzle master's messages and challenges are texted to players who have the app, which shows them anyway, as well as to those who don't. New quests text them; turning it off saves texting them.

entrants.description: The users and teams playing the quest, in order; at least one. Each has its own progress through the same stops. A player may be in only one of them, as a user or in a team. On a change, those already playing keep their progress, new ones start out not started, and those left out are removed, which is allowed only before they start.

cardWord.description: A word or phrase printed large on the stop's QR card, for a mini-game in which the players put the cards' words together. Empty removes it; left out, it stays as it is.

post.summary: Text a team's members
post.description: Sends the puzzle master's message to the entrant's players; the entry must be in progress. It's kept with the entry, which players see in the app (and players with the app are sent it as a push notification), and texted, a few seconds apart as carriers require, to the players who accept text messages, unless the quest's textPlayersWithApp is false, which leaves out those with the app. With an expected response it sets a challenge, which the entry waits for its players to answer, in the app or by text; a right answer shows them the confirmation. The challenge is kept with the quest, so challengeId can send it to the next entrant. Refused (noRecipients) if no player has the app or accepts texts. Not found if the team isn't one of the quest's entrants.

post.description: Sends the puzzle master's message to the entrant's players; the entry must be in progress. It's kept with the entry, which players see in the app (and players with the app are sent it as a push notification), and texted, a few seconds apart as carriers require, to the players who accept text messages, unless the quest's textPlayersWithApp is false, which leaves out those with the app. With an expected response it sets a challenge, which the entry waits for its players to answer, in the app or by text; a right answer shows them the confirmation. Not found if the player isn't one of the quest's entrants.

An entry that hasn't started shows its status, with no puzzles. While the quest is a race that not every entry has finished (racing), anyone but staff and administrators sees only the standings, with no stops (stopsHidden), so rivals can't read each other's puzzles and answers; and a signed-in player whose own entry hasn't completed the quest sees only that entry (rivalsHidden), until it has. The entries come in leaderboard order, each with its rank once it has completed, and the ranks are provisional until every entry has. A private quest is not found, except by its players (in any of its entries), its staff, and holders of a share link.

What anyone may see of a puzzle once an entry's players have activated it: what it asks, the hints that entry revealed, and the solution, once that entry solved it. A puzzle the entry hasn't activated, or an entry the quest doesn't have, is not found; so is every puzzle while the quest is a race that not every entry has finished, except for staff and administrators.

statusDescription.description: The status in English words, for display; the wording may change, so act on status instead.

activationCode.description: The code that unlocks the stop, which staff show the players as a QR code.

skipped.description: True if an administrator skipped the stop for the entry, completing it with no penalty, rather than its players solving it.

hintsRevealed.description: How many of the puzzle's hints the entry has revealed.

hintCount.description: How many hints the puzzle has.

activationTime.description: When the entry activated the stop; null until it has.

startTime.description: When the stop became the entry's next, to find and activate; null until it has.

endTime.description: When the entry completed the stop; null until it has.

timePenaltySeconds.description: Seconds revealing it adds to the players' time.

solutionWarning.description: True if the hint gives the solution away, so a client can warn first.

NextHint.description: What revealing the puzzle's next hint would cost.

entryId.description: The ID of the quest's entry whose progress changed: a quest can have several users or teams playing it, each with its own progress.

questComplete.description: True when it was the quest's last puzzle: the entry has completed the quest.

LiveUpdate.description: A message from the live-update websocket, /api/v1/updates, to a client: which kind is in its message field.

ticket.description: A ticket from POST /quests/{questName}/live-tickets, which can be used once.
A ticket from POST /users/{userName}/live-tickets, which can be used once.

LiveUpdateSubscription.description: The message a client sends to the live-update websocket: with questName, to follow every update of a quest; with userName, to hear when the list of quests the user plays changes. Sending another follows that instead. A ticket that isn't valid for it closes the connection.

category.description: The kind of notification. Later versions may add kinds; an app ignores one it doesn't know.

questName.description: The quest it's about. Tapping it opens the quest.

puzzleName.description: The puzzle it's about, where there is one: for stopSolved, the stop solved.

title.description: Its title: the quest's display name.

body.description: What happened, in English, written by the server.

PushNotification.description: What a push notification carries. On iOS, title and body are the APNs alert, the other fields are custom keys beside aps, and the quest is the thread-id. On Android, title and body are the FCM notification, the other fields are its data (strings), and the quest is its tag. A notification never shows a solution or a hint, never says how many stops a quest has, and never tells a racing player about a rival's progress.

shareLink.name: X-Share-Token
shareLink.description: A share link's token, which lets its holder follow a private quest.

sessionCookie.name: pq-session
sessionCookie.description: The session cookie a browser gets on signing in.

bearer.description: The session token an app gets on signing in with client "native".
